archmage.defaultWhen: The book attack is enabled and no specific team problem justifies giving up the kill.
archmage.defaultRisk: A direct attack can hit protection or a visitor trap. Retrain changes real abilities and can break an ally’s established cover.

alternatives.label: Retrain for a specific team need
alternatives.when: The current composition cannot solve a named obstacle, or an ally has agreed that replacing their ability is worth losing this ordinary kill.
alternatives.action: Use Retrain on yourself or an agreeing ally; choose an available legal Coven role that solves that problem.
alternatives.targetRule: Name the missing utility first. Another ally can receive only an eligible Common Coven role; self-Retrain has broader valid choices.
alternatives.reason: A deliberate role change can add lasting utility, while a random replacement can remove the very ability the team needed.
alternatives.pivot: If the desired role is unavailable, the ally declines, or a useful kill matters more tonight, return to the attack plan.
goals: Agree which ability the team needs
Check the offered replacement is legal
Record which role will actually act next night
laterPriorities: Verify the role change actually resolved
Build the next team plan around the replacement
Update the public cover when future movement changes
alternatives.risk: Retrain and the ordinary book attack are alternative actions. Do not promise both; do not silently replace an ally’s useful role.

hex-master.defaultWhen: You are Hexing without the book and can mark a living opponent the team expects to leave alive.
hex-master.defaultRisk: Every death can change the completion count. A successful mark on tonight’s kill usually contributes less lasting progress.

alternatives.label: Use the astral book attack
alternatives.when: You hold the book and the team needs a kill more than slow progress on surviving Hex targets.
alternatives.action: Choose the best reachable enemy for the combined Hex and book attack.
alternatives.targetRule: An exposed useful enemy with direct-visit protection can be attractive because this attack is astral; Powerful Defense can still stop its Basic damage.
alternatives.reason: Astral targeting avoids ordinary visitor interception, so it can solve a kill route a direct attacker cannot safely use.
alternatives.pivot: If the target survives and remains Hexed, update the live count; do not count an attack attempt as a guaranteed kill.
laterPriorities: Use astral access against suitable protected houses
Preserve survival if the Hex Bomb is near
Reassess the remaining unhexed player after each death
alternatives.risk: The action no longer looks like an ordinary visiting Cleric or Psychic. Astral does not mean stronger attack or immunity to every investigation.

witch.defaultWhen: You lack a confirmed role to exploit, so information plus a safe nonally destination has the best general value.
witch.defaultRisk: The controlled player knows Control happened. Hangover blocks consecutive Control, and the second selection is their destination, not a second personal visit.

alternatives.label: Redirect a known protector
alternatives.when: You have reliable reason to think an enemy has useful targeted protection and want to divert it from the team’s intended victim.
alternatives.action: Control that protector toward an eligible ally or another destination the team wants protected.
alternatives.targetRule: Keep the controlled player as your first selection. Pick the second destination for the actual protective ability, including restrictions and visitor danger.
alternatives.reason: This can both strip the enemy’s intended protection and use the displaced protection for Coven.
alternatives.pivot: Change the plan if they are Hungover, immune, out of uses, or the redirected action did not resolve.
goals: Keep first target and redirected destination separate
laterPriorities: Rotate around Hangover
Use learned roles to choose valuable redirections
Do not expose extra role knowledge in a cover will
alternatives.risk: Some abilities cannot be forced and special-button behavior differs. A protected ally is not automatically saved; the controlled player can report being Witched.

alternatives.label: Exploit a known dangerous visitor
alternatives.when: You know an enemy’s usable attack or other consequential visit, and have a specific destination where it benefits Coven.
alternatives.action: Control that enemy toward a useful nonally; coordinate a Jinx trap only if that visitor and house create a sensible ambush.
alternatives.targetRule: Never direct a dangerous action into an ally for convenience. Check that the first target can actually perform the action tonight.
alternatives.reason: A known ability is more valuable than random redirection because you can predict what the forced destination changes.
alternatives.pivot: If the target cannot act, is immune, or is Hungover, choose a different eligible actor rather than repeating the same Control.
goals: Choose a safe destination for Coven
laterPriorities: Exploit confirmed role knowledge
Share genuine stolen feedback privately
Reassess book damage against the first target
alternatives.risk: A Werewolf or Serial Killer interaction can be lethal. Your personal footprint is still the first selected player; do not claim two Seer visits.

conjurer.defaultWhen: You do not hold the book. There is no separate night ability, so your meaningful choice is the later Meteor timing.
conjurer.defaultRisk: Meteor has one use, a distinctive public death event, and no D1 use. It cannot demonstrate a Deputy shot.

alternatives.label: Take an enabled book kill
alternatives.when: You actually hold the Necronomicon and the team has assigned you its night attack.
alternatives.action: Coordinate a Basic attack on one useful nonally while retaining the unused day Meteor.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose a reachable enemy rather than a likely direct-visit trap. Grace Period can make an N1 attack unavailable.
alternatives.reason: Using the book supplies real night kill value without spending the separate one-use day resource.
alternatives.pivot: If the night action is disabled, hold it; reassess the Meteor at the next legal day window instead.
laterPriorities: Use Meteor when it changes the day outcome
Avoid duplicating an inevitable execution
Update a nonvisiting cover before later visible attacks
alternatives.risk: A night book kill is a direct visit. You cannot retroactively present Meteor as a normal Deputy shot or count night protection as daytime safety.

ritualist.defaultWhen: There is no well-supported exact legal role, so preserve both scarce Ritual attempts.
ritualist.defaultRisk: Wrong guesses still spend a charge. TI and Illuminated players are ineligible, and an alignment such as TP is not an exact role.

alternatives.label: Spend a supported Ritual
alternatives.when: A valuable non-TI target has a reliable exact role and is not currently Illuminated.
alternatives.action: Use Blood Ritual with that exact role after checking eligibility and the team’s plan.
alternatives.targetRule: Prefer a verified or strongly supported exposed enemy. Do not substitute a role-family guess or stale role information after a possible change.
alternatives.reason: A correct legal Ritual is an astral Unstoppable attack, which can solve protection a Basic book attack cannot.
alternatives.pivot: If Illumination or uncertainty appears, keep the attempt and use a different legal plan.
goals: Verify exact role rather than alignment
laterPriorities: Spend only on supported eligible enemies
Recheck role changes before reusing information
Keep the unused book alternative distinct
alternatives.risk: Even a correct guess cannot kill Invincible Defense. A wrong guess creates no usable result and still costs a charge.

alternatives.label: Use the book instead of guessing
alternatives.when: You hold the book but lack a good legal Ritual guess, or a Basic attack is sufficient.
alternatives.action: Select the ordinary book attack against a useful reachable enemy.
alternatives.targetRule: Check direct-visit protection and choose a target whose death helps the team; do not guess just to use the more unusual button.
alternatives.reason: A coordinated Basic attack can advance Coven while preserving both Ritual attempts for better role information.
alternatives.pivot: If a high-confidence protected legal target emerges, compare an actual Ritual before submitting the final action.
laterPriorities: Reserve Rituals for exact-role opportunities
Track book ownership and visit evidence
Reassess the cover when switching from astral to direct action
alternatives.risk: The book attack is an alternative to Blood Ritual and creates a normal visit. Do not claim both resolved that night.

jinx.defaultWhen: You can predict useful enemy visitor traffic without creating a crowd of surviving witnesses; otherwise a nonbook hold is reasonable.
jinx.defaultRisk: The passive attack hits one eligible non-Coven direct visitor, not every visitor, and surviving direct visitors can identify you. Normal Coven allies are excluded; Town Traitor is an exception.

alternatives.label: Coordinate one predictable visitor
alternatives.when: A Witch knows a useful eligible enemy visitor and can legally redirect them into your chosen house.
alternatives.action: Agree a house and a controlled enemy visitor, then Jinx that house without adding unnecessary allied or public traffic.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose a non-Coven resident and a visitor worth attacking. Both players must have a legal, working action; do not treat a control attempt as certainty.
alternatives.reason: One planned enemy visitor can be a better ambush than hoping a crowded protection call contains the right target.
alternatives.pivot: If the Witch target is Hungover, immune, protected, or cannot make the visit, choose a different route or hold.
goals: Check the expected visitor can move
Plan for a witness who survives
laterPriorities: Prefer predicted enemy traffic over random houses
Reassess immediately after identity exposure
Coordinate the book and remaining visitor value
alternatives.risk: The visitor can survive Basic damage and identify you. Coven visitors are normally spared by the passive attack, but their presence does not make the cover believable.

alternatives.label: Prioritize the book’s direct kill
alternatives.when: You hold the book and a useful target kill matters even if no visitor ambush occurs.
alternatives.action: Attack the chosen nonally with the book; treat the possible visitor attack as an additional conditional benefit.
alternatives.targetRule: Pick a reachable enemy first. Add visitor value only when there is evidence, rather than sacrificing the important kill for speculative traffic.
alternatives.reason: Late in a game, a reliable direct kill can matter more than an ambush that nobody visits.
alternatives.pivot: If direct protection makes the kill poor or surviving witnesses will decide the next vote, compare another target with the team.
goals: Plan the next day if identified
laterPriorities: Use actual kill feedback to update the plan
Avoid calling the resident protected
Spend survival and vote control deliberately after exposure
alternatives.risk: Book attacks can trigger direct protective retaliation. A Jinx death label or witness is not explained away by calling yourself Crusader.

dreamweaver.defaultWhen: A useful Town target seems relatively unlikely to receive a Town visit on the following night.
dreamweaver.defaultRisk: Dreamwoven is a pending effect, not immediate Insomnia. A later Town cure, your death, or Retrain can remove the disruption.

alternatives.label: Coordinate denial of a likely cure
alternatives.when: The team has access control or communication disruption that can meaningfully reduce a particular target’s next-night cure.
alternatives.action: Dreamweave that useful Town target, then coordinate the next night’s Smog or an appropriate Silence plan to make the cure harder.
alternatives.targetRule: Use a target whose lost ability matters. Confirm that any Smog does not obstruct the team’s own important visit plan.
alternatives.reason: The delayed payoff is more achievable when the team plans around the following night rather than simply marking a busy public hub.
alternatives.pivot: If a Town astral cure or visible cure removes the pending state, record that failure and choose a new plan.
goals: Agree how to reduce cure traffic
laterPriorities: Check actual cure or progression
Avoid duplicating disruption on an already disabled enemy
Stay alive if persistent Insomnia matters
alternatives.risk: Smog does not block every astral Town action. Silence hides communication rather than physically preventing a cure.

alternatives.label: Make the book kill
alternatives.when: You hold the book and removing a reachable enemy now has more value than selecting only for delayed Insomnia.
alternatives.action: Choose the combined book attack and Dreamweave target for immediate kill value.
alternatives.targetRule: Avoid an ally and weigh actual defense. Retain earlier pending targets in private notes instead of assuming they disappeared.
alternatives.reason: A dead enemy no longer contributes abilities or votes; the delayed effect should not distract from the team’s enabled kill.
alternatives.pivot: If damage fails, keep the real pending effect and its potential cure separate from the unsuccessful kill.
goals: Confirm the direct attack is enabled
laterPriorities: Prioritize live threats with the book
Track survivors who may still progress
Do not invent an immediate roleblock result
alternatives.risk: The direct attack can expose your visit and the distinctive dream effect still does not supply the protection promised by a TP cover.

enchanter.defaultWhen: A plausible investigation target exists and you have no specific coordinated death forgery to justify spending Alterate.
enchanter.defaultRisk: A frame needs a detection channel to matter. It does not rewrite Tracker, Lookout, Spy, or Coroner observations.

alternatives.label: Forge a planned death
alternatives.when: The team expects a particular victim to die and a coherent false role, faction, and will would change Town’s next decision.
alternatives.action: Use Alterate with an internally consistent public story tied to the agreed victim.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose a credible victim with a realistic death plan. Check that the forged claims and results fit earlier public events.
alternatives.reason: Deleting or replacing a real information trail can be worth a scarce forgery charge when it causes a concrete misleading inference.
alternatives.pivot: If the kill is unlikely or a Medusa mark will take priority, preserve the charge instead.
goals: Check the false will against public facts
laterPriorities: Keep later public claims consistent with the forgery
Expect unaffected observers to challenge it
Avoid spending charges on speculative survivors
alternatives.risk: A charge can be wasted if the victim lives. Stone Gaze can supersede the displayed forgery, and Coven knowledge is not the same as Town’s view.

alternatives.label: Use the book to make the death happen
alternatives.when: You hold the book and a direct kill or attack-plus-forgery plan is more valuable than a frame alone.
alternatives.action: Choose a reachable enemy for the book attack; add Alterate only if a remaining charge has a useful coherent purpose.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose for kill value and actual defense before choosing the false death story.
alternatives.reason: An enabled attack can turn a death forgery from a guess into a more concrete team plan.
alternatives.pivot: If protection or an obstacle prevents the death, retain that actual outcome rather than presenting the intended forgery as completed.
goals: Check whether a forgery charge is worth spending
Separate intended and actual death information
laterPriorities: Reconcile forged evidence with later claims
Do not dismiss unaffected observations as Enchant
Recheck book ownership and remaining charges
alternatives.risk: Book damage is Basic and can fail. An invented personal investigation is still invented even if the target was genuinely Enchanted.

illusionist.defaultWhen: One ally is carrying out the team’s most exposed important action, usually the active book holder.
illusionist.defaultRisk: Illusion is astral and hides from some investigations; current rules do not let it bypass Bodyguard, Trapper, or Deputy.

alternatives.label: Spend Phantasm on broad detection pressure
alternatives.when: Several Coven members face meaningful detection pressure tonight and one Illusion cannot cover the important risk.
alternatives.action: Use the single Phantasm charge for the eligible faction-wide Illusions.
alternatives.targetRule: Name the allies and detection channels this protects. A lone vague worry is a reason to keep the charge.
alternatives.reason: The scarce teamwide ability is worth spending when it covers several real risks at once.
alternatives.pivot: If only one important ally is threatened, return to ordinary Illusion and preserve Phantasm.
goals: Keep the actual book attacker coordinated
laterPriorities: Exploit the protected information window
Remember unaffected observers and protective counters
Keep Disguise consistent with the public cover
alternatives.risk: Phantasm excludes Town Traitors. Illusion does not make an ally safe from every form of observation or direct protective retaliation.

alternatives.label: Attack with the book instead
alternatives.when: You hold the book and the team needs your direct kill more than an Illusion that night.
alternatives.action: Choose the actual book attack against a useful nonally and verify the final selected mode.
alternatives.targetRule: Avoid direct-visit traps; choose a target whose removal matters.
alternatives.reason: An important kill can outweigh concealment, but it changes your own movement and the cover you can sustain.
alternatives.pivot: If you decide to Illusion instead, actively select that mode; do not assume canceling one automatically restores the other.
laterPriorities: Switch back to Illusion when another ally attacks
Expect direct visit evidence after book nights
Keep the chosen death Disguise coherent
alternatives.risk: Illusion and the ordinary book attack are alternative actions. A direct attack is not covered by claiming an astral Oracle history.

medusa.defaultWhen: The team has a credible kill plan and hiding that victim’s role or will has useful information value.
medusa.defaultRisk: Stone Gaze is a permanent mark, not an immediate kill. You have three active charges and already start Stoned yourself.

alternatives.label: Mark an important future victim
alternatives.when: Tonight’s agreed kill is unlikely to land, but a different informative enemy is likely to die later.
alternatives.action: Place one persistent Stone mark on that future victim after agreeing why hiding their later information matters.
alternatives.targetRule: Prefer a useful information holder expected to die eventually; do not re-mark an existing target.
alternatives.reason: A permanent mark can still pay off on a later death, so the target need not die the night you visit.
alternatives.pivot: If the player is likely to survive indefinitely or the charge has no foreseeable information value, keep it.
goals: Confirm the target is not already marked
Name the information you want hidden
laterPriorities: Coordinate a later meaningful kill
Avoid duplicate marks
Distinguish a marked survivor from a completed concealment
alternatives.risk: You grant no protection and do not learn a living target’s role simply by marking them. Later death or observer evidence may connect the visit.

alternatives.label: Hold when no useful death plan exists
alternatives.when: You have no credible victim or no reason that concealment would help the team.
alternatives.action: Save the active Stone charge and help plan the team’s next informative kill.
alternatives.targetRule: Do not select a random house just to create a visiting will line. If you hold the book and can attack, compare that real kill separately.
alternatives.reason: A limited charge kept for a meaningful death is worth more than one spent without a useful consequence.
alternatives.pivot: Once a useful likely death emerges, choose a fresh mark or a coordinated book attack.
goals: Prepare a cover consistent with holding
Identify which enemy information is dangerous
laterPriorities: Spend marks for actual information denial
Keep prior marks in the plan
Reassess after book ownership changes
alternatives.risk: Holding produces no direct visit. Do not write a performed Barrier or Psychic target as though matching movement has been established.

necromancer.defaultWhen: A normal fresh N1 has no usable corpse and you are not making a book attack.
necromancer.defaultRisk: Retributionist overlap only works with a corpse and destination that Town Retributionist could legally use. Dead evil or Stoned bodies break that overlap.

alternatives.label: Use the book’s direct attack
alternatives.when: You hold the book and no available corpse action offers greater immediate value.
alternatives.action: Choose a useful nonally for the ordinary book attack rather than inventing a corpse action.
alternatives.targetRule: Check direct-visit protection. On N1, a direct attack can be useful even though the graveyard is empty.
alternatives.reason: The book supplies immediate kill value when your ordinary ability has no resource to use.
alternatives.pivot: When a useful corpse becomes available, compare that ability against the book attack for the next night.
goals: Confirm which night mode is selected
Keep the empty graveyard chronology honest
laterPriorities: Use eligible Town corpses for a sustained Ret cover
Reassess before using evil or Stoned corpses
Keep each corpse’s actual uses and availability
alternatives.risk: You cannot perform an ordinary book attack and Reanimate in the same night. A visible living-player attack does not match an empty Ret night.

poisoner.defaultWhen: A useful enemy night actor can be Drunk and there is no coordinated reason to block access to a different house.
poisoner.defaultRisk: Hangover prevents a consecutive roleblock. Immune targets still act, and an uncautious Serial Killer can retaliate.

alternatives.label: Smog a specific access route
alternatives.when: Stopping incoming visits at a house helps the team more than blocking the resident’s own action.
alternatives.action: Smog that house after coordinating every planned allied visit and the intended enemy visit to deny.
alternatives.targetRule: A Dreamwoven target awaiting a cure or a house receiving known protective traffic can be useful. The resident’s own action is not roleblocked by Smog.
alternatives.reason: Access denial can prevent a cure or protection route that ordinary Drink would leave open.
alternatives.pivot: If an essential allied action is blocked too, change the house or use Drink instead.
goals: Name the incoming visit to deny
laterPriorities: Track obstacles without inventing visitor identities
Coordinate the next needed kill or cure denial
Change routes as enemy traffic adapts
alternatives.risk: Smog can obstruct Coven visits, including interactions that otherwise look astral; Ritual is a documented exception. It is not a complete Socialite guest-list system.

alternatives.label: Combine book damage with a roleblock
alternatives.when: You hold the book and an enabled enemy kill is the highest-value action.
alternatives.action: Use the book attack on a useful nonally; the action also attempts to roleblock that resident.
alternatives.targetRule: Pick an enemy whose death or stopped action matters, checking actual immunity and defense.
alternatives.reason: This can remove a target and interrupt their action rather than spending the night on access denial.
alternatives.pivot: If damage fails, preserve the distinction between the blocked action, immunity, and the failed kill.
goals: Keep Smog off the same-night plan
laterPriorities: Rotate around Hangover and immunity
Use Drink when another ally should attack
Avoid treating no Coven death as proof a blocked target is the killer
alternatives.risk: You cannot use ordinary Smog and the book attack together. Retaliation and direct protection can still matter.

potion-master.defaultWhen: No ally faces a concrete immediate threat, so one unresolved useful enemy role is worth Revealing.
potion-master.defaultRisk: Reveal grants Illumination, which temporarily stops Ritualist from using that information for a Ritual. Knowing a role does not grant its action history.

alternatives.label: Barrier an ally under real threat
alternatives.when: Keeping a valuable ally alive now matters more than one extra role reveal.
alternatives.action: Use Barrier on that ally and record genuine attack/save feedback.
alternatives.targetRule: Prefer an ally with concrete danger and important remaining utility, not a random recipient. Self-Barrier is possible outside its documented endgame restriction.
alternatives.reason: A real Powerful Barrier can preserve an important teammate and genuinely support part of a Cleric story.
alternatives.pivot: If the threat disappears or would bypass Powerful Defense, compare Reveal or the team’s book plan.
goals: Know what Powerful Defense can stop
Keep actual feedback separate from a guessed save
laterPriorities: Protect important remaining utility
Return to Reveal when no concrete threat exists
Do not imply every potion night supplied Barrier
alternatives.risk: Barrier cannot stop Unstoppable damage. Repeated self-protection does not match a Cleric’s single self-Barrier allowance.

alternatives.label: Use the Harmful Potion
alternatives.when: You hold the book and the team needs your enabled kill more than protection or information.
alternatives.action: Select the Harmful Potion against a useful nonally.
alternatives.targetRule: Check the destination’s actual defense and direct-visit dangers; do not target an ally or assume Reveal and Barrier also resolve.
alternatives.reason: An enemy removed now may matter more than a role learned or an ally protected without a threat.
alternatives.pivot: If another ally should carry the kill, coordinate that plan and select one genuinely useful utility potion instead.
laterPriorities: Switch potions for real team needs
Account for book nights in the cover
Preserve verified role information without leaking it as impossible TI results
alternatives.risk: One selected potion is one action. A kill night is not also a genuine Cleric save or Sheriff investigation.

voodoo-master.defaultWhen: You lack a reliable investigative target and a useful nonally is likely to contribute to the next day’s discussion.
voodoo-master.defaultRisk: Silence suppresses communication, not the night ability. The same player cannot receive any doll on consecutive nights.

alternatives.label: Blind a known information role
alternatives.when: A credible enemy investigator or other feedback-dependent player is likely to produce consequential results tonight.
alternatives.action: Choose Blind on that player to suppress that night’s visible feedback and results.
alternatives.targetRule: Prefer a supported useful information role over an unknown chatty player; check the previous night’s target regardless of doll mode.
alternatives.reason: Denying a real report can be more valuable than Silence when you know where the information will come from.
alternatives.pivot: If the target has no useful feedback to deny, is your previous target, or is acting in a way Blind will not stop, return to another legal disruption.
goals: Identify the result you want to deny
laterPriorities: Rotate to useful fresh information targets
Coordinate day pressure around missing reports
With the book, plan damage plus the selected effect
alternatives.risk: Blind does not stop the player from acting. A protection or attack can still resolve even when the recipient sees no result.

alternatives.label: Deafen a coordination-dependent opponent
alternatives.when: An enemy needs to receive claims or whispers to coordinate the next day, and preventing their replies is less valuable than denying incoming information.
alternatives.action: Choose Deafen on that player and let the team plan around the disrupted communication channel.
alternatives.targetRule: Use an organizer or player relying on private coordination; they must be a different player from your last doll target.
alternatives.reason: Deafen can isolate a coordinator from new discussion while they remain able to speak.
alternatives.pivot: If the objective is to stop public reporting use Silence; if it is to deny night results use Blind instead.
goals: Name the incoming communication to deny
Remember the target can still speak
laterPriorities: Choose the doll for the next specific obstacle
Avoid treating Deafened speech as proof the effect failed
Reassess book damage and target legality
alternatives.risk: Deafen does not mute the player or roleblock them. It is narrower than a complete communication shutdown.

wildling.defaultWhen: A useful enemy’s outgoing action is likely to provide a clear, limited Tracker-style report.
wildling.defaultRisk: Sense shows visible movement, not every astral action, and also gives extra information a Tracker cover must keep private.

alternatives.label: Build a real Lookout account
alternatives.when: Incoming traffic at a useful house is more informative than following its resident’s destination.
alternatives.action: Sense that house and keep only the visible visitor-identity channel in the public Lookout account.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose a house likely to receive strategically useful visits without knowingly entering a lethal traffic trap. Do not select yourself as though normal Lookout permits self-Watch.
alternatives.reason: Real visitor observations give more support than invented protective claims when the traffic channel is the valuable one.
alternatives.pivot: If useful evidence mainly concerns outgoing movement, keep the Tracker route instead; do not blend both roles’ outputs in one will.
laterPriorities: Report only the visible visitor channel
Do not infer exact roles from visitor identity
Reassess if the book attacks the same watched target
alternatives.risk: A missing name is not proof nobody visited astrally. Book damage and private whisper knowledge can expose information beyond the claimed role.

alternatives.label: Kill while retaining Sense
alternatives.when: You hold the book and the team wants a direct attack more than observation of a survivor.
alternatives.action: Attack and Sense the same useful nonally target; retain the actual movement feedback.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose a valuable reachable enemy, recognizing the book forbids an allied target and removes the option to observe a different house at the same time.
alternatives.reason: You retain real information while performing the team kill, so the night is not observation-only.
alternatives.pivot: If the direct visit is too dangerous or a different observation is essential, coordinate book ownership before assuming both actions can split.
goals: Separate the kill from the observed channel
laterPriorities: Keep only the cover’s permitted information
Use surviving traffic to refine later choices
Expect death details to challenge a quiet observation story
alternatives.risk: Sense and the book attack share a target. An accurate report does not turn the associated attack into a Town ability.

covenite.defaultWhen: Another ally is already using the book effectively and you have no independent night ability.
covenite.defaultRisk: An empty night has no natural effect evidence. A low-writing claim can still require public proof later.

alternatives.label: Carry the team’s book
alternatives.when: Giving you the book frees a stronger ally’s utility, and the team accepts the direct attacker’s exposure risk.
alternatives.action: Coordinate book ownership and attack a useful nonally if the kill is enabled.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose a reachable enemy while useful allies spend their own actions on utility. Never assume you have the book simply because this is your preferred route.
alternatives.reason: Using the otherwise idle Covenite for the ordinary kill can preserve the team’s more valuable specialist actions.
alternatives.pivot: If another book holder has a specific superior attack route, let that plan take priority and remain available for later.
goals: Agree who actually holds the book
Keep utility allies free to act
laterPriorities: Take book work when it preserves better utility
Reassess traps and defense before attacks
Update the public footprint after each action
alternatives.risk: Being expendable does not make a bad attack good. Book ownership and direct traffic still constrain the plan.

alternatives.label: Trade cover longevity for early pressure
alternatives.when: The team needs a plausible public case or a deliberate trade more urgently than your long-term quiet survival.
alternatives.action: Prepare a restrained TI cover before the night, using coordinated real team knowledge only where the claimed role and movement could explain it.
alternatives.targetRule: Choose one interpretable unresolved enemy. Do not invent an impossible N1 visit while you actually stayed home.
alternatives.reason: A less valuable specialist can sometimes take the social risk of a contested case, leaving stronger allies a safer path.
alternatives.pivot: If there is no supported story or the case would expose several teammates, keep the lower-pressure cover instead.
goals: Post a coherent limited report early
laterPriorities: Reassess when the target’s role becomes known
Do not leak secret role information as a magical result
Keep the next book action consistent with the actual plan
alternatives.risk: This is a riskier discussion route, not a new Covenite ability. A fabricated result can cause an immediate execution and is not evidence-based confirmation.

cultist.defaultWhen: You are not attacking with the book and lack a useful supported Town recruit worth spending the one conversion on.
cultist.defaultRisk: Indoctrinate is a daytime action, changes faction without replacing the recruit’s role, and removes your Basic Defense once successful.

alternatives.label: Carry the book while preserving conversion
alternatives.when: You actually hold the book and a useful enabled kill advances Coven more than remaining idle tonight.
alternatives.action: Attack a useful nonally; retain Indoctrinate for the next legal day opportunity with a worthwhile Town recruit.
alternatives.targetRule: Pick for reachable kill value and avoid destroying the only useful intended recruit without considering the trade.
alternatives.reason: The ordinary night kill and the scarce day conversion solve different problems; keeping the charge does not require wasting an available attack.
alternatives.pivot: When a supported valuable Town recruit emerges, reassess conversion before the day vote or ability window closes.
goals: Verify book ownership and kill availability
Keep the recruit list separate from the kill target
laterPriorities: Recruit useful Town ability or vote value
Plan around losing your initial defense
Keep the recruit’s real role and new faction separate
alternatives.risk: A surviving attack before conversion is not proof of a Town protective role. The direct book visit also breaks an Oracle-shaped no-visit story.
